title: Inverse scalar cocycle and units for the specified integral associators
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. For every finite $F\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $\mathcal I_F^s(T)$ and $\mathcal I_F^p(T)$ be the framework and PBC integral full categories underlying [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $I_F$ be their exact integral identity identification, as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,T}$, and for $E\subseteq L$ write $C_{L/E}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ for ordinary derived extension and $U_{L/E}$ for the strict quotient-tower extension [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Integral formulas below are written in the common full categories using $I_F$.
Suppose the actual maps $b_{L/E}=\chi_{L/E}$ restrict to natural isomorphisms $C_{L/E}\to U_{L/E}$, with ordinary coefficient-presentation transport fixing tensor generators. Write $A^C_{M,L,E}:C_{M/L}C_{L/E}\to C_{M/E}$ for ordinary derived tensor balancing, and $A^U_{M,L,E}$ for the specified integral framework associator, normalized by conjugation of that same balancing by these same completion maps [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization, lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator]. For $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$ and every integral $K$, the equations in the derived category are
$$A^U_K\,U_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K})\,b_{M/L,C_{L/E}K}=b_{M/E,K}\,A^C_K,$$
$$A^C_K\,C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K}^{-1})\,b_{M/L,U_{L/E}K}^{-1}=b_{M/E,K}^{-1}\,A^U_K.$$
Here composition is read right to left. The first equation uses the actual quotient cocones, is independent of K-flat representatives, and is an equation for the chosen framework associator. Under ordinary presentation transport, $A^C$ is the integral balancing whose rationalization is the specified PBC associator [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].
Let $\mu_E:C_{E/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be tensor multiplication and $\eta_E:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{E/E}$ the completeness unit. Then $b_{E/E}=\eta_E\mu_E$, so $\mu_E b_{E/E}^{-1}=\eta_E^{-1}$ is the normalized inverse unit. The inverse equation respects the two associator unit laws for these multiplication/completeness identifications. In particular its substitutions $L=E$ and $M=L$ are the two unit comparison squares, and $E=L=M$ is their identity square. All statements allow repeated fields adjacent to strict extensions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator] on $T$ to the actual maps $b=\chi$. Its normalization is precisely $A^U_K U_{M/L}(b_{L/E,K})b_{M/L,C_{L/E}K}=b_{M/E,K}A^C_K$, after the given identity identifications. Its statement supplies actual quotient cocones, independence of K-flat representatives, and unit laws. Its derived-complete-input hypothesis holds because the given integral categories consist of derived-complete objects. The assumed normalization identifies the chosen framework associator with this one; it does not replace it by an arbitrary isomorphic map.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; agent-written expansion of old proof steps 4–6: integral associator, inverse cancellation and units.

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], integral ordinary change of completed coefficient rings restricts and rationalizes to the PBC scalar functor, whose specified associator is derived tensor balancing. Under the assumed ordinary presentation transport, balancing sends $(x\otimes l)\otimes m$ to $x\otimes lm$ on either presentation: the transport fixes the generators and coefficient multiplication. Thus the $A^C$ in step 1 rationalizes to that specified PBC associator.

proof.text: For this step abbreviate $C_1=C_{L/E}$, $C_2=C_{M/L}$, $U_1=U_{L/E}$, $U_2=U_{M/L}$, and $b_1=b_{L/E}$, $b_2=b_{M/L}$, $b_3=b_{M/E}$. Naturality of $b_2$ at $b_{1,K}^{-1}:U_1K\to C_1K$ gives $b_{2,C_1K}C_2(b_{1,K}^{-1})=U_2(b_{1,K}^{-1})b_{2,U_1K}$. Hence, putting $D=U_2(b_{1,K})b_{2,C_1K}$, we obtain $C_2(b_{1,K}^{-1})b_{2,U_1K}^{-1}=b_{2,C_1K}^{-1}U_2(b_{1,K}^{-1})=D^{-1}$. Step 1 says $A^U_KD=b_{3,K}A^C_K$. Multiplying on the left by $b_{3,K}^{-1}$ and on the right by $D^{-1}$ gives $A^C_KC_2(b_{1,K}^{-1})b_{2,U_1K}^{-1}=b_{3,K}^{-1}A^U_K$, exactly the claimed inverse equation. This uses only functoriality, naturality and inverse cancellation in the common derived category.

proof.text: The identity-extension clause of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies $\chi_{E/E}$, after tensor multiplication, with the natural completeness map. As $b=\chi$ and this input is complete, this says $b_{E/E}=\eta_E\mu_E$ as natural isomorphisms. Inverting gives $b_{E/E}^{-1}=\mu_E^{-1}\eta_E^{-1}$ and therefore $\mu_Eb_{E/E}^{-1}=\eta_E^{-1}$. This uses the independently specified completeness unit, not a new choice of it.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; agent-written expansion of old proof steps 4–6: integral associator, inverse cancellation and units.

proof.text: For $L=E$, write $C=C_{M/E}$, $U=U_{M/E}$ and $b=b_{M/E}$. The stated unit laws of [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator] and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] identify $A^C_K=C(\mu_{E,K})$ and $A^U_K=U(\eta_{E,K}^{-1})$. The left side of the inverse equation is consequently $C(\mu_E)C(b_{E/E}^{-1})b_{M/E,U_{E/E}K}^{-1}=C(\eta_E^{-1})b_{M/E,U_{E/E}K}^{-1}$. Naturality of $b^{-1}$ at $\eta_{E,K}^{-1}:U_{E/E}K\to K$ identifies this with $b_{M/E,K}^{-1}U(\eta_{E,K}^{-1})$, its right side. This is the first unit comparison square.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; agent-written expansion of old proof steps 4–6: integral associator, inverse cancellation and units.

proof.text: For $M=L$, write $C=C_{L/E}$, $U=U_{L/E}$ and $b=b_{L/E}$. The same unit laws give $A^C_K=\mu_{L,CK}$ and $A^U_K=\eta_{L,UK}^{-1}$. Substituting step 4, the left side of the inverse equation becomes $\mu_{L,CK}C_{L/L}(b_K^{-1})\mu_{L,UK}^{-1}\eta_{L,UK}^{-1}$. Naturality of $\mu_L$ at $b_K^{-1}$ reduces this to $b_K^{-1}\eta_{L,UK}^{-1}$, its right side. This is the second unit comparison square. With all three fields equal, step 4 identifies $b^{-1}$ with $\mu^{-1}\eta^{-1}$; after these multiplication/completeness identifications both unit squares have identity edges, giving the identity square. No argument used strictness of an inclusion: all repeated-field cases, including repetitions adjacent to a strict inclusion, are covered.
